title: Getting started with arulesNBMiner
text: paper models item’s frequency Poisson count item specific rate, models variation rates Gamma distribution. Mixing Poisson counts Gamma rates gives negative binomial distribution. flexible baseline captures skewed frequency distributions common transaction data: items occur often, many occur rarely. NBMinerParameters() estimates global model item frequencies. Items never occur absent transactions, estimator uses expectation-maximization procedure estimate unobserved zero frequency class. trim argument can exclude frequent items outliers distort fit. Inspect diagnostic plot choosing nonzero trim value.  figure compares observed cumulative item frequencies frequencies expected fitted baseline. estimate scaled per incidence NBMiner, described paper.
code: param <- NBMinerParameters(Agrawal.db,                             pi = 0.99,                             theta = 0.5,                             maxlen = 5,                             minlen = 1,                            trim = 0,                             verbose = TRUE,                             plot = TRUE) #> using Expectation Maximization for missing zero class #> iteration = 1 , zero class = 3 , k = 0.9862909 , m = 277.9777  #> iteration = 2 , zero class = 3 , k = 0.9862909 , m = 277.9777  #> total items =  719 param #>    pi theta   n         k           a minlen maxlen rules #>  0.99   0.5 719 0.9862909 0.001371754      1      5 FALSE

title: Getting started with arulesNBMiner
text: itemset already found, NBMiner considers adding possible item. fits baseline transactions containing itemset predicts many extensions reach frequency chance. pi parameter sets minimum predicted precision accepting extensions. , precision means predicted proportion accepted extensions true associations model; guarantee actual precision every data set. theta parameter controls search pruning. larger itemset, sets required fraction immediate subsets must support itemset NB-frequent pattern. value 1 restrictive; 0 relaxes condition. intermediate value 0.5 used balances pruning chance retaining associations whose items different frequencies. maxlen limits longest itemset considered, minlen can set minimum length returned patterns. control list accepts verbose debug logical options. Results include model-estimated precision precision quality column. comparison, add support measure.
code: itemsets <- NBMiner(   Agrawal.db,   parameter = param,   control = list(verbose = FALSE, debug = FALSE) )  quality(itemsets) <- cbind(quality(itemsets),                            support = interestMeasure(itemsets, "support",                                             transactions = Agrawal.db))  inspect(head(sort(itemsets, by = "support"), n = 10)) #>      items     precision support #> [1]  {item446} 1         0.08190 #> [2]  {item938} 1         0.07570 #> [3]  {item818} 1         0.07250 #> [4]  {item457} 1         0.06985 #> [5]  {item401} 1         0.06945 #> [6]  {item453} 1         0.06895 #> [7]  {item355} 1         0.06880 #> [8]  {item238} 1         0.06765 #> [9]  {item615} 1         0.06720 #> [10] {item318} 1         0.06220

text: R package extends arules NBMiner, implementation model-based mining algorithm NB-frequent itemsets described Michael Hahsler’s paper, “model-based frequency constraint mining associations transaction data.” Data Mining Knowledge Discovery, 13(2):137–166, September 2006. package also supports mining NB-precise rules.
